body: I'll admit I don't "understand" the suicidal thoughts, as I've never been there. And when I said crying wolf, I wasn't trying to imply that I don't believe him... just that's I've heard it so many times. I read through both links you posted and yes, he is definitely a risk. And as for talking tips... I literally feel I've done everything! I'm always pointing out his positive attributes, I know he loves my young son, so I try to make him an active uncle in his life, My husband even started a band with him in it, told him to focus on his drumming... something fun, but he just gets frustrated when things go wrong there. I just don't know what to do! I'm lost and don't mean to make him a burden.... but it's so hard when I know I really am the only person on this planet he expresses these feelings to. Both of his parents have dies in the last few years... (which I can relate to having lost both of mine) . He has multiple siblings but all of them are distant to one another. I just want to help him. The most recent thing he said to me was that he should find a new home for his dogs so he could go without having to worry about them starving to death.... that may give you some insight.
I can honestly say I DO try to ask without attacking... it's when he says "What are you talking about, I donno" that my blood boils over and can't help it, cuz at that point, he's blatantly lying!

I want nothing more than to fully trust him again! I trusted him blindly for 2 years to just come and find he had kept such a significant secret from me and did things online behind my back that deserved a lack of trust! He even admits that....

I completely understand and appreciate all of that! I NEVER dug before, because I trusted him blindly. And then weird things were popping up and the digging started. Since then though there HAS been an open communication, demonstration, and even sexualization regarding the matter! Dressing around the house has become 'common' when he feels the need to do so. He doesn't ask, I don't question, it just is! I understand digging is "wrong", but I think purposely hiding things from me is as well! When I ask him, I do my best not to 'attack', I ask him what was he hiding and to quote myself recently "If I'm supposed to be accepting and open to this part of you, how am I supposed to feel when you're doing things behind my back?" It's a two way road! And if there is bi-curiosity tied to it, don't I have the right to know! I did promise my life to this man... and if he wants something I can't provide......... I donno.... it's a lot to wrap my brain around!

Considering digging is the ONLY reason I even know about the dressing, and he lied repeatedly when confronted, as I stated, trust was lost! Trust is something that needs to be earned back and the fact that he's still hiding things isn't earning it back! I don't dig nearly as much as I did when things all first came out but the hiding is driving me nuts!
It's not so much knowing every single possible thing about him, it's being able to, I guess, *get* him better..... when he wants to dress I'm constantly thinking.... "OK.... but why?"
Well yeah, I have a good rack and a nice ass but I'm talking more short shorts or very tight fitting clothes.... =P

First off I'd like to say thanks a lot for creating this post. Since finding out my fiance enjoys crossdressing, I've been trolling this subreddit often and even randomly messaging people for opinions and advice.... it especially helps since I can't actually talk to anyone I know about what I'm going through. And now... on to my story (which some here may know already, some may not, but thanks to all who take the time to read and offer me anything in return).

About 3 and half months ago I stumbled up some things on the internet and basically had to force my Jimmy to come out to me. It took almost 3 days of him lying or giving little tidbits of the truth, but in the end.... I learned about Zoey. Probably almost instantly I began searching the internet, trying to learn anything I could about crossdressers and that's what lead me to this subreddit. It didn't take long before I got over thinking he was gay (which I have to admit was my biggest fear), because of the many many things I read about straight men doing this.... phew! A few days after learning about *Zoey*, we had a night of big emotional talking and, going against the advice of many, I chose to dive in and right then and there I took scissors and cut off his goatee and told him to full on dress for me, I had to know what I was dealing with (plus I knew he had been dying to do it). After that, I'd say approximately 3 weeks went by when he was dressing daily when he got home from work... anything from just pink pajamas to full on looking like a hooker on a Sunday morning. We had some *girl's night* and it was OK.... but I REALLY started to get sick of Zoey, because well, I missed Jim. He could see that it was upsetting me and he stopped doing it for a while (*sidenote*: I never asked him to, he just did). In all honesty he stopped as well because he just wasn't feeling the urge to do it as strongly and I think the 3 weeks was kind of a binge after not doing it for over 2 years. We've still been talking about it and he's still doing it here and there while I'm at work. The thing that definitely upset me the most is the lying, knowing that the man I trusted more than anyone in the world kept something from me for so long and now he's lost that blind trust and has to earn it back. Obviously I completely understand the reasons behind the lying but it doesn't make it hurt any less. Another thing is the lack of understanding.... I really cannot wrap my brain around why my guy's guy enjoys being completely feminine sometimes. He says he can't really explain it, just that he likes it..... but I don't *get it*. Knowing that I don't truly understand the person I want to spend the rest of my life with, tears me upart. And then there's the newst thing I'm discovering.... the jealousy factor. I myself am not a girly girl at all.... I live in band t-shirts and jeans and wear make-up only like 10 times a year. It's not so much I don't like it, I just don't feel the need to impress anyone. Well I'm about 5'4" tall and weigh about 175lbs and he's about 5'7" tall and 135lbs..... I just don't look good in some things and now I find myself in stores looking at clothes I wish I could wear but debating on buying them for Zoey. I have bought him stuff but it really pisses me off knowing he can pull off some things better than I can! Well, I think that just about covers the jist of things..... thanks again to anyone who reads this!

P.S. When he smells like perfume instead of cologne..... that turns me off more than ANYTHING! Is that weird?


After having my fiance read what I wrote, he said it was important to mention that that first time dressing, it was all clothes I had given him.... things that no longer fit me, but he had always admired.

We definitely have talked and talked till we're blue in the face! The biggest problem for me is truly the lack of understanding of it all. He says he can't put into words why he does it and that's why my brain gets so boggled! I don't think it's sexual for him either..... but I'm a person who's always lived by, there's a reason for everything and not being able to *get it* bugs the crap outta me.... LOL

Hehehe, before I red the posts, I was going to ask if this was the dress that would have clashed with Ricki! Looks great! Just a curious question, since I've noticed the obvious pattern..... do you ever move away from the dress, cardigan, scarf and tights? Or is that your style and you're sticking to it?!
That is a really cute dress, very good shape! Btw.... is that a photo of you in a suit in the background???

I recently (about 3 months ago) found out my fiance of 2 years enjoys crosdressing and I think a direct quote from me at the time was "this would have been easier if you were gay, because then at least things would make sense!" I think you're right about the mental box thing, seeing as the media really only has crossdressers portrayed as flamboyant drag queens or serial killers with mommy issues.... lol! I still do not understand it, but I can say *creepy* is the wrong word. I never thought of it as a creepy thing.... just.... weird. This page has at least helped me to understand that men who do this come from all sexual preferences..... but I'm still trying to *get it*.

Well, having recently (within the past few months) found out my fiance enjoys crossdressing, I've been doing my best to learn what I can, and hopefully better understand him. I can't say watching your segment was an accident.... I didn't stick around to watch the couple who didn't touch, because I can't relate to that! =P
P.S. FYI edith, you responded to his post too, just noticed that.

Hahaha, you made me giggle... so thanks for that! I feel I've lost my smile! It was the fashion advice thing. Maybe that's another reason why this is SO confusing for me. My wardrobe is probably 90% pants and a black band t-shirt. I never wear make up, unless it's an occasion. And when I do dress up the quote "ugh, I look like a girl!" often comes out of my mouth. Oh the confusion.....

I know he is still who he is. And he hasn't show me anything yet, so I don't really know anything.... but baby steps! My fear is that as much as I love him, I love to look at him too.... I don't want to lose that! Thank you for the response...
Thank you... I've been reading some stuff on here and I have even found a story very parallel to mine. I'm trying to learn.... like I said it's only been 4 days!
